turns.q: After the thousand years, is Satan released?
turns.reply: Yes. Revelation 20:7-10 says: "And when the thousand years are expired, Satan shall be loosed out of his prison, And shall go out to deceive the nations which are in the four quarters of the earth, Gog and Magog, to gather them together to battle: the number of whom is as the sand of the sea. And they went up on the breadth of the earth, and compassed the camp of the saints about, and the beloved city: and fire came down from God out of heaven, and devoured them. And the devil that deceived them was cast into the lake of fire and brimstone, where the beast and the false prophet are, and shall be tormented day and night for ever and ever." Revelation states that Satan shall be loosed after the thousand years.

And they went up on the breadth of the earth, and compassed the camp of the saints about, and the beloved city: and fire came down from God out of heaven, and devoured them. And the devil that deceived them was cast into the lake of fire and brimstone, where the beast and the false prophet are, and shall be tormented day and night for ever and ever." Revelation says Satan shall be loosed; it does not explicitly name who looses him. Revelation 20:1-3 earlier describes an angel binding Satan; applying that binding agent to the later release is inference, not the wording of the release statement.

turns.q: When is the first resurrection relative to the thousand years?
turns.reply: Direct answer: In the first resurrection, God’s people who are Christ’s are raised to life and reign with Him; Revelation 20:4-6 calls this the first resurrection, with 1 Thessalonians 4 and 1 Corinthians 15 describing the gathering of the dead in Christ. Scripture witnesses: Revelation 20:4-6; 1 Thessalonians 4:13-17; 1 Corinthians 15:51-54; John 5:28-29.
